clue.text: Invited to go to a university to make music at dawn

indicators.note: the word for invited is told to go after the a and the university, so it comes last

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, so it means invited or asked

explanation.surface: Someone is asked along to a university to play music in the early morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go to' places BADE after A and U.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a song or piece of music greeting the morning, the opposite of a serenade.

clue.text: Girl without employment — one seen at the airport?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the girl's name goes around the word for employment

parts.note: Carol is a girl's name
use means employment, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: A jobless girl is wondering whether someone she spotted at the airport is relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense of outside, so the girl surrounds the employment word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating belt that delivers luggage in an airport baggage hall is called a carousel.

clue.text: Get into big trouble with digital devices?

definitions.text: Get into big trouble with digital devices?

parts.words: Get into big trouble with digital devices?
parts.note: the idiom for suffering from a risky venture is read literally: fingers are digits, so something digital could scorch them

explanation.surface: Someone lands in serious bother through their gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital devices' suggests computers and phones, but digits are fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to suffer unpleasant consequences from meddling or taking a risk.

clue.text: A moment of the month we are in

definitions.meaning: a very brief moment of time

definitions.text: of the month we are in
definitions.meaning: in old business letters 'inst.' or ... meant the current month, as in 'your letter of the 5th ...'

explanation.surface: Someone notes a moment in the current month.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is old-fashioned commercial jargon, abbreviated inst.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a brief point of time and, in dated correspondence, the present calendar month are meanings of the word.

clue.text: Public benefactors on hip pal's t-shirt possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could form something else when rearranged

parts.note: the s here counts as a letter of the fodder
the hyphen is ignored, giving six letters

explanation.surface: Charitable donors are described as printed on a trendy friend's top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ONHIPPALSTSHIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: Philanthropists are people who give money generously to good causes for the benefit of society.

clue.text: Mister jumping across river to get cat

indicators.note: the two letters for mister straddle the river, one on each bank

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, a favourite crossword river

explanation.surface: A man leaps over a river to fetch a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping across' puts M and R either side of OUSE; the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire and elsewhere in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat kept for, or good at, catching mice.

clue.text: Take care of mum — medical state not good

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
ma is an informal word for mother, like mum

explanation.surface: A carer is told to look after their mother, whose medical condition is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take care of' looks like an instruction to nurse someone; only 'care of' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, clearly a bad medical condition.

clue.text: Committee of adjudicators one short on a Scottish island

indicators.note: the word for the panel loses one letter, its last

parts.note: a jury is a panel of people judging a case or competition

explanation.surface: A judging panel, one member down, convenes on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one short' trims the panel word to JUR before A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Jura is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast, famous for its whisky.

clue.text: Vessel to merit being mentioned

indicators.note: being mentioned means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to earn something is to merit or deserve it

explanation.surface: A pot is so good it deserves a mention.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a large vase or container, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Bird with two rings seen by end of lake

parts.note: a hoop is a ring
the letter O is shaped like a ring

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word lake

explanation.surface: A bird wearing two rings is spotted at the edge of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two rings' gives two different rings: HOOP and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested bird with a distinctive call, found across Europe, Asia and Africa.

clue.text: Infant taken short with nothing on, the monkey!

indicators.note: taken short means cut off before its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a baby is an infant
O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naked toddler caught needing the loo is called a little monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken short' is British slang for urgently needing a toilet, but here it trims BABY to BAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A baboon is a large African monkey with a dog-like muzzle.

clue.text: Charm shown by church composer, half-hearted fellow

indicators.note: the composer's heart is the double L in the middle, and half of it is lost

parts.note: Thomas Tallis was a Tudor composer of English church music
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A lucky charm is displayed by a lukewarm church musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two central Ls in TALLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring luck or protection, like an amulet.

clue.text: Anna's top groaner — sadly somebody who isn't welcome

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters are in a sorry, jumbled state

parts.note: here the s counts as a letter

explanation.surface: Anna's best moaner is unfortunately someone people would rather not see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges ANNASTOPGROANER.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for an unwelcome person, used chiefly of a diplomat expelled by a host country.

clue.text: Pull in a particular direction

definitions.meaning: to haul a vehicle or boat behind on a rope
read as two words, '...' means towards the west, a particular compass direction

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: split the answer as TO W, heading westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauling along behind is one sense; split as 'to W', it says heading west, a specific compass bearing.

clue.text: Not making a profit makes one perplexed

definitions.meaning: a business trading below cost is losing money

explanation.surface: Running a business in the red leaves someone baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both selling below cost and being bewildered or stuck for an answer.

clue.text: Greek character is endlessly tense

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taut means tightly stretched, tense

explanation.surface: A figure from Greece is forever nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to T.

clue.text: Dim, like the opposition spokespeople?

definitions.meaning: faint, poorly lit, full of shade
in British politics the main opposition party names a Shadow Cabinet of spokespeople who mirror government ministers

explanation.surface: Opposition spokespeople are mocked as rather dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The British opposition's frontbench is called the Shadow Cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure and murky in light, and also resembling the Shadow Cabinet of opposition politicians.

clue.text: Nice things to eat, as in diet properly controlled

indicators.note: the letters are taken in hand and put into a proper order

explanation.surface: Treats are allowed, as part of a well-managed eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properly controlled' rearranges ASINDIET.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainties are delicacies, small tasty treats.

clue.text: Selfishness gets "moi" into trouble

indicators.note: getting into trouble means getting into a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Saying 'moi' all the time lands someone in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into trouble' rearranges GETSMOI; 'moi', French for 'me', fits the surface of self-regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotism is excessive concern with oneself and one's own importance.

clue.text: Financial institution contributing to the general welfare?

definitions.meaning: a British mutual lender of mortgages, owned by its savers
read literally, constructing a better community for everyone

explanation.walkthrough: A building society is a British savings and mortgage lender, like a US savings and loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A British mutual mortgage lender, and literally the act of strengthening the community.

clue.text: Frequently conveyed outside and tossed into the air

indicators.note: outside says the word for conveyed sits around the word for frequently

parts.note: led means guided or conducted, conveyed
oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: Something often carried around is then flung upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveyed outside' reads as carried out of doors; it is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lofted ball has been struck high into the air, as in golf or cricket.

clue.text: The heart — someone showing everything's OK?

definitions.meaning: slang for the organ that beats, like a clock
one who marks items with a check mark to approve them

explanation.surface: A doctor checks the heart and gives a thumbs up.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a tick is the mark Americans call a check.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the beating organ, and literally a person who puts approval marks on a list.

clue.text: Action at a high level

parts.note: sounds like boardroom activity, but means combat up in the sky between aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'high level' suggests senior management; it is literal altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerial combat between fighter planes takes place high in the sky.

clue.text: Instrument an 'omeless person heard

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a homeless wanderer is a hobo, and the apostrophe drops the H as in a Cockney accent

explanation.surface: A homeless person is heard playing an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in ''omeless' tells you to drop the H of HOBO too.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Untouched by way of diplomacy

parts.note: in can mean by way of or through, as in 'in that way'
tact is sensitivity and diplomacy in handling people

explanation.surface: Something is left unharmed through careful diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means whole and undamaged, left alone.

clue.text: One won't succeed on one's own

definitions.text: One won't succeed on one's own

parts.words: One won't succeed on one's own
parts.note: sounds like a failure needing help, but succeed means inherit, and this person shares the inheritance

explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' means take over an estate or title, not achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint inheritor shares an estate with others rather than inheriting alone.

clue.text: Rested? That's the day the lord did!

definitions.text: That's the day the lord did!
definitions.meaning: the short form for Saturday, the Jewish Sabbath, the day of rest after God's six days of creation

explanation.surface: A remark that resting on the day God took off is only right.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is SAT, short for Saturday, the original Sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: Being seated is a way of resting, and the abbreviation for Saturday names the Sabbath, the day of divine rest.

clue.text: Said to employ sheep

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: to use something is to employ it

explanation.surface: Someone claims they hire out sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewes are female sheep.
